events.title: Charles VI grants Roquefort-sur-Soulzon a monopoly on its cheese
events.description: King Charles VI of France granted the people of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon a monopoly on ripening Roquefort cheese, as they had done for centuries. The sheep's-milk blue cheese took its name from the commune.
events.html: King Charles VI of France granted the people of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon a monopoly on ripening Roquefort cheese, as they had done for centuries. The sheep's-milk blue cheese took its name from the commune.

events.title: Osaka Castle falls and the Toyotomi line ends
events.description: As Tokugawa forces took Osaka Castle, Toyotomi Hideyori and his mother took their own lives. The Tokugawa shogunate faced no serious rival for the next 250 years.
events.html: As Tokugawa forces took Osaka Castle, Toyotomi Hideyori and his mother took their own lives. The Tokugawa shogunate faced no serious rival for the next 250 years.

events.title: Frederick the Great defeats an Austro-Saxon army at Hohenfriedberg
events.description: In the Second Silesian War, part of the War of the Austrian Succession, Frederick the Great's Prussian army decisively defeated an Austro-Saxon army under Prince Charles Alexander of Lorraine. It was one of Frederick's most admired victories.
events.html: In the Second Silesian War, part of the War of the Austrian Succession, Frederick the Great's Prussian army decisively defeated an Austro-Saxon army under Prince Charles Alexander of Lorraine. It was one of Frederick's most admired victories.

events.title: Montgolfier brothers fly a hot-air balloon in public
events.description: In the market square at Annonay, Joseph and Étienne Montgolfier launched an unmanned linen balloon that rose some 2,000 metres. Human flights followed before the year was out.
events.html: In the market square at Annonay, Joseph and Étienne Montgolfier launched an unmanned linen balloon that rose some 2,000 metres. Human flights followed before the year was out.

events.title: Suffragette Emily Davison is struck by the King's horse at Epsom
events.description: During the Derby, Emily Wilding Davison stepped onto the course and was knocked down by Anmer, George V's horse. She died four days later and became a martyr of the suffrage movement.
events.html: During the Derby, Emily Wilding Davison stepped onto the course and was knocked down by Anmer, George V's horse. She died four days later and became a martyr of the suffrage movement.

events.title: Churchill vows 'we shall fight on the beaches'
events.description: As the Dunkirk evacuation ended, Churchill told the Commons it was not a victory but promised that Britain would 'never surrender'.
events.html: As the Dunkirk evacuation ended, Churchill told the Commons it was not a victory but promised that Britain would 'never surrender'.

events.title: US dive-bombers wreck Japan's carrier force at Midway
events.description: Within minutes American dive-bombers set three Japanese carriers ablaze; a fourth was hit that afternoon. Japan lost its best carriers and many experienced aircrew.
events.html: Within minutes American dive-bombers set three Japanese carriers ablaze; a fourth was hit that afternoon. Japan lost its best carriers and many experienced aircrew.

events.title: Solidarity sweeps Poland's semi-free elections
events.description: Solidarity won all but one of the freely contested seats. The result led to the first non-communist-led government in the Soviet bloc and began the fall of communism in Eastern Europe.
